residual_risks: The same-body existing central-sectional-area report explicitly lists crossing polygon vertices; evaluating its side lengths is an elementary computational consequence. Novelty is not claimed for the raw crossing construction, but for the combined sharp perimeter bound, quantitative stability and nonsmooth axis law.

value.rationale: Maximum intrinsic central-section perimeter of the standard FCC Voronoi rhombic dodecahedron is a natural convex-geometric invariant. The complete directional perimeter function and unique optimizer orbit complement, but are not the same as, existing area laws. The tetrahedral tight-frame deficit gives a global nontrivial quantitative inequality, while the exact cusp separates linear section response from quadratic projected-perimeter response at the sharp maximizers. The result yields reproducible section-perimeter benchmarks with nontrivial geometric boundaries; no broader independent theorem is claimed.
